# Batteries offline source carrier

The canonical Git-managed location is
`third_party/batteries/batteries-v4.33.0.bundle`. The distribution builder uses
this path by default, resolved from its checkout rather than the current working
directory. An explicit `--batteries-bundle PATH` remains supported; both paths
must satisfy the selected dependency lock's exact byte length and SHA-256.

The verified bundle is present in this directory for ordinary Git retention,
with no ignored-cache or LFS dependency. `.gitattributes` preserves its bytes
across platforms. The November 4 recovery regenerated it from the exact pinned
source and independently verified a clean offline clone and complete history.

The [recovery record](../../Plans/batteries-recovery-20261104/README.md) and
[carrier receipt](../../Plans/batteries-recovery-20261104/carrier.json) retain
generation provenance: Git 2.53.0, `pack.threads=1`, `pack.compression=9`,
and `git bundle create ... HEAD` in an isolated clone. The generated bytes
match the earlier retained `f6efbfeb…` carrier. This does not establish general
cross-host reproducible generation.

The October 31 [re-pin](../../Plans/batteries-bundle-repin-evidence-20261031/README.md)
selected a different carrier, `73130433…` / 3,739,542 bytes. Those original bytes
were not recovered from the accessible environments. The user authorized
recovery if lost, and both current dependency locks now select the verified
replacement above at the unchanged source revision/tree. Historical receipts
retain their original pins and qualification limits.

Verify from the repository root:

```sh
sha256sum --check third_party/batteries/SHA256SUMS
```

Bundle integrity, clean offline clone, exact revision/tree, license identity,
and complete history have been verified by the recovery record. Repeat those
checks when admitting another copy; the checksum does not replace Git identity
checks. A different carrier requires a separately reviewed re-pin.

The location/default change and carrier re-pin do not qualify the previous
frozen candidate. A new source/candidate freeze must bind the resulting tracked
tree and dependency locks before new distribution or framework acceptance.
